criteria.text: Identifies the automatic renewal problem in Distribution Agreement Section 2.2 (read with the Section 1.1 definition of Renewal Term): non-renewal notice is allowed only in a narrow window (no earlier than 120 and no later than 90 days before term end), and renewal terms run five years, which is longer than the four-year Initial Term. Explains that one missed window locks Glakin in for five more years.
hints: 120 days and not later than 90 days

criteria.text: Identifies that Glakin's right to object to the 9% cartridge price increase under Distribution Agreement Section 5.4 has lapsed. The notice was delivered July 20, 2026 (Amendment No. 1 Recital B), the 45-day objection period ended on or about September 3, 2026, and Amendment No. 1 (dated September 14, 2026) does not preserve or revive the right. The increase is therefore deemed accepted.

Identifies that the non-compete in Distribution Agreement Section 3.3 is broader than the agreed exclusivity in SOW Section 1.2. Section 3.3 covers any veterinary diagnostic product or service anywhere in North America, while SOW Section 1.2 covers hematology analyzers and cartridges in the U.S. only. Explains that the Distribution Agreement prevails over the SOW under Section 19.4, so the broader restriction controls.

Identifies that Quality Agreement Section 9.4 makes Sumeith's recall and quality-nonconformity liability 'subject to Section 11.2' (the cap). Explains that because the Quality Agreement prevails on quality matters under Distribution Agreement Section 19.4, this overrides the uncapped recall/quality carve-out in Distribution Agreement Section 11.3 and caps Glakin's recovery of recall costs.

Identifies that Amendment No. 1 Section 3 adds a new Section 12.3 requiring Glakin to indemnify Sumeith for Regulatory Claims with no fault or negligence standard. Also notes that the same section amends Section 11.3 to exclude this indemnity from the liability cap, so Glakin's exposure is uncapped.
States the order of precedence in Distribution Agreement Section 19.4 as: Amendment first, then the Quality Agreement (for quality matters), then the Distribution Agreement, then the SOW.
States that the Distribution Agreement liability cap in Section 11.2 is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
Is presented as a memo addressed to the supervising partner, and for each issue gives the document and section, why it matters for Glakin, and a recommended fix.
Prioritizes or ranks the issues by importance or urgency, and flags which points should be raised with the client directly.
Does not conclude that Glakin can still timely object to the 9% price increase under Section 5.4, or that the objection window was still open on the Amendment date.
Does not conclude that the SOW's narrower hematology-only, U.S.-only exclusivity scope controls over Distribution Agreement Section 3.3.
hints: Distribution Agreement prevails over the SOW
